request.summary: Create a custom portal for approval requests currently handled through inconsistent email and chat flows.
request.desired_outcome: Create a traceable request-to-decision flow with consistent inputs and visible status across four departments.

necessity_basis.statement: Some approval outcome appears necessary, but the basis for each approval route was not supplied.

normal_path: Requester sends a request through email or chat
An approver reviews through an inconsistent route
exceptions: Approval paths vary by request and department, but legitimate exception types are unknown
simplification_opportunities: Remove approval steps that lack a confirmed policy or control purpose

facts.statement: Requests arrive through email and chat.
Different templates and approval routes are used.
Four departments submit an estimated 20–40 requests per month.
No owner for the end-to-end process was named.

interpretations.statement: Building now would encode disputed or undocumented approval rules.

assumptions.statement: A portal would reduce lost status and inconsistent submissions.

constraints.statement: The solution must support work across four departments.

unknowns.question: Which approval outcomes and routes are mandatory?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Unnecessary approvals should not be standardized or automated.

unknowns.question: Can the existing work-management suite support the minimum process?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Existing capability may avoid procurement or custom ownership.

unknowns.question: Who will own the process and any future solution?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Rules, exceptions, support, and changes need an accountable owner.

evidence_tasks.question: Which approvals are mandatory and who owns the policy?
evidence_tasks.why_it_matters: This determines which parts of the process are necessary.
evidence_tasks.action: Review the governing policy or control with its accountable owner.
evidence_tasks.completion_evidence: A named owner and source-backed list of mandatory approval outcomes.

evidence_tasks.question: What is the minimum stable approval model?
evidence_tasks.why_it_matters: A tool needs shared request categories, inputs, routes, and exception rules.
evidence_tasks.action: Map recent synthetic or sanitized cases into a normal path and legitimate exception set.
evidence_tasks.completion_evidence: Agreed request categories, required fields, approval rules, status definitions, and exception owners.

evidence_tasks.question: Can the current work-management suite support the minimum model?
evidence_tasks.why_it_matters: An owned capability may be faster and cheaper than buying or building.
evidence_tasks.action: Configure a sanitized test flow using the minimum model and record fit and gaps.
evidence_tasks.completion_evidence: Capability test with supported requirements, gaps, workarounds, and ownership implications.

evidence_tasks.question: Who will own operation and change after launch?
evidence_tasks.why_it_matters: No technology option is sustainable without process, support, and lifecycle ownership.
evidence_tasks.action: Assign or escalate ownership for process decisions, support, change, and technology lifecycle.
evidence_tasks.completion_evidence: Named accountable owners and an accepted support/change path.

options.rationale: The necessary outcome may be real, but request definitions, routes, exceptions, and ownership are unstable.

critical_conditions.consequence: A reviewer must confirm who can standardize the process and accept changes.

options.rationale: The existing suite may fit, but the minimum process and capability test are missing.

critical_conditions.evidence: Required routes and exceptions are not defined.
critical_conditions.consequence: Capability fit cannot be assessed responsibly.

options.rationale: The differentiated capability, lifecycle owner, and total-cost inputs are absent.

critical_conditions.evidence: No software lifecycle owner was identified.
critical_conditions.consequence: Do not commit to a custom build at the current stage.

scores.rationale: The coordination problem is plausible, while the mandatory outcome is not fully established.
Process redesign directly addresses inconsistent definitions and routes.
Clarifying the minimum model can begin without software delivery.
Process work avoids premature software lifecycle cost.
The work can surface ownership, but no owner is currently named.
Forms and status may support the desired outcome.
Fit is mixed until routes and exceptions are defined.
An owned tool may be quick to configure, but it has not been tested.
Existing ownership may reduce incremental cost, subject to confirmation.
Not assessed because current tool and process ownership are unknown.
A portal might help, but custom capability is not tied to verified differentiated value.
A build would encode unstable routes and definitions.
Development and operational setup add lead time.
Not assessed because no cost horizon, rates, or operating model were supplied.

scorecard.ranking_caveat: Weights are requester drafts and critical policy, process-fit, and ownership evidence is unresolved.

responsibilities.notes: No end-to-end process owner was named.
No delivery team or capacity was supplied.
Data and control requirements are unknown.
Systems and sources of truth were not identified.
No support or transition path was supplied.
No lifecycle owner or exit path was supplied.

limitations: Vendor research is premature until the minimum approval model and existing capability are assessed.

recommendation.rationale: The approval outcome may be necessary, but inconsistent definitions, routes, exceptions, and ownership would make a tool decision premature.
caveats: The monthly volume is an estimate.
The mandatory approval basis has not been supplied.
Existing capability has not been tested.
blocking_conditions: No confirmed process or policy owner.
No agreed minimum request and approval model.
No assessment of the existing work-management capability.
recommendation.next_decision: Confirm the minimum approval model and then decide whether the existing suite is sufficient for a bounded trial.

handoff.brief_markdown: The approval outcome appears necessary, but the current process is not stable enough for a responsible custom-build decision. Confirm mandatory approvals and ownership, define the minimum request and exception model, and test the existing work-management suite. Then compare process-only, existing-capability, integration, buy, and custom paths using reviewer-confirmed priorities.
